target_customer: AI startups that sell into industries run on legacy Windows desktop software with no API (healthcare, logistics, finance and similar)
problem: AI products cannot go live because customers' systems of record are desktop apps without APIs, and scripted automations break often.
business_model: Usage-based API and platform for self-healing desktop automations on Windows VMs
product_category: Desktop automation infrastructure for AI companies

founders.name: Faizaan Chishtie
prior_employers: Early engineer at YC startups (per YC page)
founders.background_notes: Education not listed on the YC page.

founders.name: Saheed Akinbile
founders.background_notes: Lagos-raised engineer per Leadership.ng profile; worked on legacy integrations at Morgan Stanley and Ford per launch post.

competitors.name: Cyberdesk
competitors.what: AI computer-use agent for Windows legacy apps, plain-English workflows via API
competitors.traction_then: Launch HN focused on dental software examples

competitors.name: UiPath
competitors.what: Incumbent RPA platform for desktop automation

competitors.name: Skyvern
competitors.what: Visual automation for web portals and API-less systems

technical_complexity.rationale: Reliable self-healing automation across Windows VMs, Citrix and varied legacy UIs is hard; the company claims 93 to 96 percent click accuracy, unverified.

defensibility.rationale: Customer integrations and observability tooling create some lock-in, but computer-use models and rivals like Cyberdesk lower barriers.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent move recorded by November 2026; established RPA vendors already sell similar desktop automation.

market_need_then: AI startups selling to healthcare and logistics need access to desktop systems without APIs; the company reports 2.5M executions run and named customer logos on its site.

branding.domain_note: Uses minicor.com; the site footer shows the legal entity Laminar Run, Inc., suggesting an earlier name, but no source confirms it.

identity.voice_and_tone: Technical and plain: describe a workflow and get an API endpoint

branding.community_and_virality: Launch HN thread and DevTech list placements; no merch or fan activity found.

brand_strength.rationale: Press covers the funding and product, not the brand; the legal name differs from the brand name.

outcome_analysis: Minicor raised a $3.8M seed in October 2026, months after its Spring 2026 batch, led by IA Ventures with YC and Paul Graham. Its founders have legacy-integration experience and it shows customer logos and usage, but rivals like Cyberdesk and incumbent RPA vendors make defensibility the key question.
notes: Seed confirmed by the company newsroom link on its site plus The SaaS News and Dealroom; one VC database lists a June 2026 seed with different investors, unverified. Paul Graham participation is confirmed only through secondary reporting and the company headline. Founded year 2024 per YC page (work began in 2023).
